messages:
alex: Heads-up: ran into weird prefetch failure mode on prod-rt yesterday during a large cold-start spike. Some requests hit CPU fallback and latencies spiked. Anyone seen this pattern before?

maya: Yea saw similar on canary last week. Looks like prefetch gave up mid-stream when fragmentation crossed a threshold.

simon: Can you paste the logs? I want to see the offload decision path.

alex: Pasted minimal stack and decision trace below:

simon: ah ok. That log shows prefetch attempted to grab a contiguous staging region and failed after 3 retries, then we hit fallback-to-host path.

jen: Do we have a clear failure mode definition? "prefetch gave up" is vague. Is it OOM, fragmentation, timeout, or throttling? :thinking:

noah: From infra side, we saw host memory pressure rise ~15% during the spike. Could be both fragmentation + transient pressure.

alex: Logs: ```
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] prefetch: try=1 size=64MB pool=staging-numa0 status=ENOSPACE
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] prefetch: try=2 status=ENOSPACE
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] prefetch: try=3 status=TIMED_OUT
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] allocator: fallback host-copy path engaged
```

maya: TIMED_OUT on retry 3 suggests our retry policy + backoff isn't adaptive to fragmentation. If free memory exists but not large contiguous blocks, retries won't help.

jen: We should classify modes as: contiguous-alloc-failure (frag), transient-pressure (host OOM risk), and policy-throttle (rate limiter). Each should map to different mitigations.

simon: Agree. For frag we should try scatter-gather prefetch (split into sub-allocs) before giving up. For pressure we should prefer smaller prefetch windows and be conservative on batch prefetch. For throttle we surface metrics.

alex: Proposed triage metrics to add: prefetch_attempts_total, prefetch_fragmentation_retries, prefetch_scatter_success, prefetch_fallback_count, host_pressure_before_prefetch_pct, time_to_first_kv_ready_ms.

noah: +1. Also add an allocator-level free-run histogram (largest_free_chunk_bytes) sampled at prefetch time. That will let us see contiguous availability.

jen: Also need an invariant: before marking prefetch as "failed", record reason code and whether recovery path (scatter/slice) was attempted. Helps for postmortem.

alex: What about interfaces? We currently have alloc.prefetch(api) -> bool success. Need richer contract: alloc.prefetch(api) -> {status, reason, attempted_strategies}.

simon: That is a breaking change but we're already evolving the allocator API. We can add an opt-in verbosity flag first: prefetch_v2=true returns the richer struct.

maya: Implementation detail: scatter-gather prefetch needs to hand back multiple KV entries and reassemble the prefix cache. That touches the kvcache merge paths. Risky but doable if we instrument.

noah: For safety, suggest feature-flag rollout: enable on canary, collect metrics, then ramp. Also add a circuit-breaker so if host pressure exceeds X% we stop scatter prefills.

alex: CI bot flagged a flaky test earlier: ci-bot: "prefetch-scatter-integration.test failed 2/10 runs on main; timeout at reassembly stage."

jen: We'll need a focused unit test that simulates high fragmentation (largest_free_chunk < requested) and asserts scatter path completes and reassembly is correct. Add deterministic RNG seeds.

simon: I can prototype scatter prefetch in a small PR. Plan: 1) change API opt-in, 2) implement scatter allocator path, 3) add metrics + largest_free_chunk sample, 4) tests + canary rollout.

maya: Timeline? We should avoid touching hotpath until tests look good.

simon: Prototype in two weeks, tests in week after, canary following week.

alex: Action items: simon to open RFC sketch for prefetch_v2 + scatter plan; jen to draft metric names and instrumentation points; noah to add host-pressure telemetry; maya to design KV reassembly contract; alex will coordinate canary rollout gates.

jen: One more: add a fallback-to-retry-with-smaller-chunks strategy before full host-copy fallback. Might save latency.

alex: Agreed. We'll enumerate strategies: scatter-into-chunks, reduce-prefetch-window, delayed-retry, and immediate-host-copy. Order is frag-sensitive.

noah: I'll add a dashboard mock showing prefetch_fallback_count vs largest_free_chunk to validate.

alex: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll make the thread RFC and ping @simon when ready. :rocket:
